statement: the provenance barrier is syntactically machine-checkable

premises.note: The module import graph G = (V, E) with V = {M0..M6} (7 nodes) and E from module_import_policy allowed_edges (at most |V|^2 = 49 edges). G is finite.
forbidden_imports: M1/M2/M3 must not import M4/M5/M6. This is a finite list of forbidden (source, target) pairs.

proof_steps.label: finite-graph
proof_steps.claim: The module import graph has finitely many nodes (|V| = 7) and finitely many edges (|E| <= 49).
proof_steps.justification: V = {M0, M1, M2, M3, M4, M5, M6}, |V| = 7. E is the set of actual imports, bounded by the syntactic structure of the source files. The repository has finitely many files, each with finitely many import statements.

proof_steps.label: dfs-terminates
proof_steps.claim: Depth-first search on a finite directed graph terminates in O(V+E) time.
proof_steps.justification: Standard algorithm analysis: DFS visits each node and edge at most once, using a coloring (WHITE/GRAY/BLACK). On 7 nodes and at most 49 edges, this is a constant-time computation.
proof_steps.base_result: Cormen et al., Introduction to Algorithms, Chapter 22 (DFS on finite digraphs)

proof_steps.label: cycle-detection-decidable
proof_steps.claim: Cycle detection in the module import graph is decidable: DFS detects a back edge iff a cycle exists.
proof_steps.justification: DFS theorem: a directed graph is acyclic iff DFS produces no back edge (GRAY-to-GRAY arc). This is a decidable property on finite graphs (step 1 + step 2).

proof_steps.label: forbidden-import-scan-decidable
proof_steps.claim: The forbidden-import scan is decidable: for each file in proof/m1, proof/m2, proof/m3, scan AST imports against the forbidden list.
proof_steps.justification: Python AST parsing is deterministic and terminates on finite source files. The forbidden list is finite. Checking membership in a finite list is decidable.

proof_steps.label: forbidden-leaf-scan-decidable
proof_steps.claim: The forbidden-construction-leaf scan is decidable: regex match against a finite pattern list on finite source files.
proof_steps.justification: Regular expression matching terminates on finite input strings. The pattern list is finite. The source files are finite.

proof_steps.label: cl07-conclusion
proof_steps.claim: The provenance barrier (DAG acyclicity + forbidden-import + forbidden-leaf) is syntactically machine-checkable.
proof_steps.justification: Conjunction of steps 3, 4, 5: each check is decidable and terminates in O(|files| * |patterns|) time. The checker (checker/check_certificate.py CORE-1 handler) implements exactly these three checks.

proof_steps.label: semantic-independence-not-claimed
proof_steps.claim: CL-07 does NOT claim semantic circularity is decidable (CL-08 is [OUT]).
proof_steps.justification: The syntactic check decides whether a given import graph violates the stated policy. It does NOT decide whether the mathematical content of two theorems are abc-equivalent. The latter is undecidable in general (no general algorithm decides abc-equivalence of an arbitrary mathematical assertion). CL-08 is [OUT] and has no downstream force.
proof_steps.note: This step is explicitly required by the honesty constraints of the spec. The immutable assumption manifest must receive separate mathematical review.

non_circularity: CL-07 is a claim about algorithm decidability, not about mathematics of abc. It uses no abc triples, no K_epsilon, no Szpiro, no IUT.
